newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam buys 170,000/T diesel for 2Q in tender.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam buys 170,000/T diesel for 2Q in tender.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) bought by tender eight cargoes of diesel totalling 170,000 tonnes for deliveries between April and June, an industry source said on Tuesday.
It bought four 20,000-tonne cargoes on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Singapore and four 22,500-tonne cargoes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Vietnam basis.
The fob cargoes were bought at a 10-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes.
Shell was awarded two cargoes of either 1.0 or 0.5 percent sulphur grade, Esso was awarded a 1.0-percent sulphur cargo and Japanese trader NKK a 0.5-percent cargo.
Singapore trader Hin Leong Trading sold one cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur diesel at 95 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City.
Hin Leong also sold two cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel, while German trader Stinnes sold one 1.0-percent cargo at $1.15 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Hongai.
Unlike previous tenders, Vietnam did not buy any jet fuel or kerosene in this tender which were normally combined with some diesel cargoes.

The source said Petrolimex would take jet-kerosene fuel for its second quarter requirements from its term contract with Kuwait Petroleum Corp. Under this contract, Petrolimex takes 120,000-130,000 tonnes of jet fuel per year.
In its last quarter for first quarter delivery, Vietnam bought four combination cargoes of diesel/jet-kerosene fuel and seven single cargoes of diesel.
The fob diesel cargoes were bought at a 15-cent premium to Singapore quotes, while c-and-f cargoes were bought at a 95-cent premium to Ho Chi Minh City and at a $1.20-premium to Hongai.
